story_title: NAA20 perturbation couples recurrent CYP46A1 repression to induction of sterol-synthesis transcripts
proxy_summary: NatB/Naa20 does not phenocopy the available NatA perturbations.
proxy_why_it_matters: Although NAA20, NAA10, and NAA15 all belong to the N-terminal acetyltransferase family, Naa10 produced no FDR-significant genes and Naa15 signatures were weaker and essentially uncorrelated with Naa20, supporting NatB-specific neuronal biology rather than interchangeability among NAT complexes.

story_title: MATR3 perturbation induces an RBP state that active FUS and TDP-43 perturbations do not reproduce
proxy_summary: Most responsive classes induced a repeated Ddhd1/Atp9b/E2f4/Zkscan3/Kcnq2/Sugp2/Uggt2-positive and Rsrp1-negative core, with Gpt2 marking a stronger midbrain and GABA-biased branch.
proxy_why_it_matters: These genes provide a compact transcriptional state for Matr3 loss that is more recurrent than any single annotated pathway in the small core list.

story_title: PPP2R1A perturbation reverses sterol-transcription polarity across neuronal classes
proxy_summary: Ppp2r1a scaffold knockdown caused much larger transcriptional responses than knockdown of Ppp2r5d, Ppp2r2b, or Ptpa in matched cell classes.
proxy_why_it_matters: Human PPP2R1A and PPP2R5D are both PP2A neurodevelopmental-disorder genes, but the dataset shows that loss of the scaffold and loss of individual regulatory or activator components are not interchangeable in this short-term RNA assay.

story_title: AP2M1 and AP2S1 perturbations converge on TFRC induction and sterol repression while AP2S1 adds cortical activity-gene loss
proxy_summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the Ap2m1 signature aligned with Ap2s1 but not with several other clathrin/endocytic neighbors; App and Vps35 were weakly anti-correlated on the Ap2m1 FDR vector.
proxy_why_it_matters: The AP2M1 program should not be interpreted as a generic consequence of every endocytic perturbation, and cargo or retromer perturbations may produce distinct or even opposite transcriptomic states.

story_title: UBA5 and UFC1 perturbations converge on DDIT3 induction and ATP6V0C repression
proxy_summary: Uba5 and the UFMylation E2 Ufc1 converged strongly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
proxy_why_it_matters: Same-direction convergence between the E1 and E2 perturbations anchors the large 151 signature to the UFMylation cascade rather than to an idiosyncratic Uba5 guide effect.

story_title: CHP1 perturbation induces the sterol module that direct SREBF2 perturbation represses
proxy_summary: Dctn1, Dync1h1, and Marchf6 perturbations drive sterol genes upward, opposite to Srebf2 loss, in the same response-capable neuronal classes.
proxy_why_it_matters: The dataset contains a bidirectional sterol module: direct Srebf2 depletion decreases the pathway, while dynein/dynactin and ER-associated degradation perturbations activate many of the same transcripts.

story_title: PGK1 and GAPDH perturbations converge on OGT and nuclear-speckle transcript loss
proxy_summary: The spliceosomal perturbation Snrnp70 converged with Pgk1 over Pnisr, Rsrp1, Arglu1, Ogt, and Nrxn1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
proxy_why_it_matters: Convergence with a direct U1-snRNP perturbation strengthens the interpretation that the Pgk1 signature reports an RNA-processing or nuclear-speckle state rather than an unrelated collection of down-regulated genes.

story_title: STXBP1 perturbation produces distinct cortical, midbrain, and Pvalb transcriptional outputs
proxy_summary: L4/5 IT cortical neurons showed the broadest Stxbp1 response, downregulating several synaptic/glutamatergic transcripts while upregulating a smaller Nrsn1/Pcsk1n/Scg2/Chgb counter-module.
proxy_why_it_matters: This is the clearest cell class in which partial Stxbp1 loss propagated from target engagement to a synapse-associated gene program rather than stopping at the target transcript.

story_title: PCYT2 and SELENOI perturbations converge on sterol induction while PCYT2 lowers peptide-processing genes
proxy_summary: Srebf2 moved the shared sterol genes in the opposite direction from Selenoi/Pcyt2 and was a leading negative Selenoi signature neighbor.
proxy_why_it_matters: The inverse Srebf2 result places Selenoi and Pcyt2 upstream of a transcriptional program that depends on SREBP2 in the same neuronal class.

story_title: Acute TBR1 perturbation recurrently raises CPNE6 while splitting mature cortical projection-neuron outputs
proxy_summary: Perturbing known TBR1 partners or laminar regulators did not phenocopy the Tbr1 signature.
proxy_why_it_matters: Biochemical membership in a TBR1/CASK/FOXP network is not enough to predict Perturb-seq equivalence in these neurons; the Tbr1 signature was closer to unrelated restricted neighbors than to Cask or Foxp2.

story_title: Zbtb11 perturbation recurrently lowers Rbm28, Stx16, Acsf3, and Ndufaf1 across subcortical neurons
proxy_summary: Responding Zbtb11-perturbed neurons converged on a down-regulated mitochondrial, nucleolar/RNA-processing, and endomembrane/glycan module rather than on a single target transcript.
proxy_why_it_matters: The repeated reduction of Ndufc2, Ndufaf1, Gtpbp3, Acsf3, Rbm28, Taf1b, Stx16, Pigq, and Man2c1 connects the mouse-brain Perturb-seq signature to known ZBTB11 control of mitochondrial and RNA-processing genes while extending it to a recurring Golgi/GPI/glycan arm.

story_title: Pura perturbation raises Nefl while lowering Ogt and neighboring Igip in thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic neurons
proxy_summary: Purb and Purg perturbations did not phenocopy the Pura signature in the two Pura-responsive classes.
proxy_why_it_matters: This argues against treating PUR-domain paralogs or PURA/PURB dimers as interchangeable in this brain Perturb-seq context.

story_title: Wdr26 perturbation recurrently lowers Srrm2 alongside neuronal excitability transcripts in cerebellar and subcortical neurons
proxy_summary: The G-protein branch of WDR26 biology was not phenocopied by Gnb1 knockdown: Gnb1 showed strong self-depletion in several groups but produced almost no downstream DE and its score vector was near-orthogonal to Wdr26.
proxy_why_it_matters: WDR26 can scaffold G beta-gamma and PLCB2 in leukocytes, but the mouse neuronal Wdr26 signature is not explained by simple transcriptional depletion of the assayed G beta subunit.

story_title: Arid1a, Smarcb1, Smarcc2, and Smarce1 perturbations converge on Ptpn3-Reep2-Prkcd repression with Clstn2-Nexn induction
proxy_summary: ARID paralogs, pBAF, and SMARCA ATPase perturbations did not simply phenocopy Arid1a in the 151 cell type.
proxy_why_it_matters: This separates cBAF base-module effects from ARID1B substitution, ARID2-pBAF biology, and SMARCA2/4 catalytic-subunit perturbation, arguing that subunit identity matters even within one chromatin-remodeling family.

story_title: Nipbl, Smc1a, and Stag2 perturbations share a Ptprm-Necab2-Smtn-Adamts2 repression core but diverge at Gabra1 and Brinp1
proxy_summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Smc3's weak ranked signature was closest to Nipbl, Smc1a, and Stag2 and shared same-direction changes in several down-ranked neuronal calcium/synaptic genes.
proxy_why_it_matters: The same-cell convergence with cohesin loader/core perturbations rescues a biologically interpretable module from an otherwise weak Smc3 result.

story_title: Setdb1 perturbation induces Atf7ip, Tasor, and clustered gamma-protocadherins without an equivalent Ehmt1 response
proxy_summary: Ehmt1, the only available related H3K9 methyltransferase perturbation, did not recapitulate the Setdb1 protocadherin/Atf7ip/Tasor program.
proxy_why_it_matters: The contrast separates the Setdb1 response from nonspecific loss of a chromatin writer and is consistent with specialized HUSH/SETDB1 control of the clustered-protocadherin locus.

story_title: Ranbp2 perturbation produces Srrm2-down/Rbm15-up cortical and Grm1-Epha4-Itpr1-up cerebellar responses
proxy_summary: The engaged L5 ET response couples Ranbp2 depletion to RNA-processing and SUMO/nuclear-protein genes.
proxy_why_it_matters: The L5 ET gene set is the cleanest in-dataset bridge between measured Ranbp2 knockdown and the known RANBP2 SUMO E3/nuclear-envelope mechanism.

story_title: Rb1 and E2f4 perturbations release distinct replication and chromosome-repair arms in thalamic neurons
proxy_summary: E2f4 perturbation derepressed a one-sided mitotic, kinetochore, and DNA-repair-associated transcript program, strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
proxy_why_it_matters: The direction fits loss of an E2F4 repressor, but the genes induced in postmitotic neurons clustered in chromosome, spindle, and repair machinery rather than in a generic stress response.

story_title: Tardbp and Fus perturbations create opposite Snrnp70 responses within separable recurrent RNA-processing states
proxy_summary: A recurrent noncanonical Tardbp response module was directionally coherent across sensitive cell types: Ppp6c, Fam219a, Usp15, Brms1l, Uggt2, Gabpa, Abcc5, Fam135a, and Sec24b repeatedly increased, whereas Snrnp70 repeatedly decreased.
proxy_why_it_matters: These genes provide scalar biomarkers of TDP-43 depletion in this dataset even though most are not the famous STMN2/UNC13A cryptic-exon markers emphasized in human motor-neuron studies.

story_title: Elp1-Elp2 and Bdp1 perturbations converge on aminoacyl-tRNA-synthetase and ATF4 stress in thalamic neurons
proxy_summary: Bdp1 and Polr3b diverged in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut despite belonging to the same RNA polymerase III transcriptional system.
proxy_why_it_matters: The result argues that the Bdp1 Ddit3/aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase program is not a generic consequence of perturbing any Pol III component in the dataset and may depend on lesion strength, subcomplex architecture, or guide efficacy.

story_title: Proteasome-core and assembly perturbations couple proteasome-gene induction to loss of neuronal ion-pump and glutamate-receptor transcripts
proxy_summary: Responsive Psmc5 classes up-regulated a recurrent proteasome and ubiquitin-proteostasis module.
proxy_why_it_matters: The direction matches a compensatory transcriptional rebound after proteasome impairment and links the perturbation to its expected core function.

story_title: ANK3 perturbation lowers calcium-handling, receptor, and active-zone transcripts without a matched Cntn1, Cntnap1, or Sptan1 response
proxy_summary: Scn8a, Scn1b, and Fgf14 were weak but high-ranking same-direction signature neighbors of Ank3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
proxy_why_it_matters: The neighbor structure points back to the expected ankyrin-G/AIS sodium-channel neighborhood even though correlations were too modest to imply that sodium-channel loss alone explains the Ank3 signature.

story_title: CALM1 perturbation induces a Rasgrp2/Peg3 module opposite to CAMTA1 and not reported after CALM3 targeting
proxy_summary: Calm1 and Calm3 are not interchangeable in TH Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells despite matched knockdown and identical protein sequence.
proxy_why_it_matters: Calm1 and Calm3 encode the same calmodulin peptide, so matched target depletion might have been expected to converge; instead Calm1 triggered a many-gene Rasgrp2/Peg3/Resp18-positive signature while Calm3 was downstream-silent in the same cell type.

story_title: ADARB1 perturbation recurrently lowers Flnb across cortical, subcortical, and cerebellar neuronal classes
proxy_summary: The Flnb response is Adarb1-selective rather than a generic consequence of perturbing Adar or the AMPA-receptor substrate Gria2.
proxy_why_it_matters: Even with target engagement of Adar or Gria2 in comparator classes, Flnb did not fall, separating the Adarb1 signature from ADAR1 loss and from loss of a central ADAR2-edited receptor transcript.

story_title: MAX perturbation derepresses STAG3 and circadian E-box genes while MGA shares only the STAG3 branch
proxy_summary: Mga perturbation releases a sparse ectopic response centered on the meiotic cohesin gene Stag3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
proxy_why_it_matters: The direction of Stag3 induction matches the known MAX/MGA-ncPRC1.6 role in repressing germline and meiosis genes, extending that mechanism to a restricted neuronal Perturb-seq context.

story_title: ATP6V0C and PITPNA perturbations converge on a calcium, PKC, and secretory-transcript state in thalamic neurons
proxy_summary: Atp6v0c, a V-ATPase V0 subunit, was the strongest recurrent positive signature neighbor of Pitpna in the two main responsive cell classes.
proxy_why_it_matters: The 17-of-20 same-direction overlap with the Pitpna TH Prkcd program and Jun convergence in P MY Pineal link PITPNA loss to an endolysosomal or synaptic-vesicle acidification module rather than to phosphoinositide signaling alone.

story_title: GRIN2A raises an L2/3 NPTX2-BDNF-PTGS2 program while GRIN2B trends oppositely and significantly lowers Vgf and Kcnv1
proxy_summary: Grin2b and Grin2a were not interchangeable in L2/3 IT cortical cells; their signatures were anticorrelated and their FDR genes did not overlap.
proxy_why_it_matters: Even closely related GluN2 subunits within the same receptor family drove opposite activity-gene behavior in the same cell class, emphasizing subunit-specific downstream wiring.

story_title: EEF2 targeting induces a large Vgf, Nptx2, and Cx3cl1 trophic state in superficial cortical neurons
proxy_summary: A recurrent Vgf/Son/Ranbp2/Smpd1 module emerged across several Eef2-responsive cell types, with Vgf repeatedly induced and Uchl1/Eno2 repeatedly repressed in responsive neuronal classes.
proxy_why_it_matters: VGF is a BDNF-inducible secreted peptide precursor with synaptic functions, so its recurrence converts a generic elongation-factor perturbation into a candidate neurosecretory and synaptic-plasticity readout.

story_title: BRAF and MAP2K1 perturbations repress, whereas NF1 perturbation induces, a neuronal VGF-PTPN5-ETV5 MAPK module
proxy_summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut contains a weak Kras module that is Braf/Map2k1-like and Nf1-opposite.
proxy_why_it_matters: Although Kras rows are nominal, the sign pattern preserves a high-value hypothesis that this thalamic glutamatergic class is the only place where Kras perturbation partially imprints a RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK output program.

story_title: SIN3A targeting induces cilium and cholesterol genes while repressing spliceosome transcripts in thalamic and midbrain neurons
proxy_summary: Max, but not Myc or Mycn, was a reproducible positive Sin3a signature neighbor in the major responder cell types.
proxy_why_it_matters: SIN3A is known to be recruited by MXD/MAX-family repressors; the Max-specific convergence suggests that, in these neurons, removing Max resembles disrupting a SIN3A-linked repressor program more than perturbing Myc-family activators.

story_title: MEF2C and MEF2A perturbations resolve different cortical and thalamic neuronal outputs
proxy_summary: The two strongest cortical IT Mef2c signatures converge on a synaptic/membrane module rather than on unrelated top genes.
proxy_why_it_matters: Up-regulation of Chgb, Stac2, Gria2, and Serinc2 with down-regulation of Slit2 in both cortical IT classes, plus FDR-supported glutamatergic-synapse and receptor-regulatory genes, links the perturbation to MEF2C's known control of excitatory synapse biology.

story_title: ESRRA and PPARGC1B perturbations converge weakly on a neuronal mitochondrial axis while retaining distinct outputs
proxy_summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Esrra was the closest positive Ppargc1b signature neighbor and co-depleted metabolic genes including Idh3b, Uqcrc1, Mdh1, and Dlst.
proxy_why_it_matters: The dataset gives an exploratory in situ echo of the known PGC-1beta-ERR connection in the same cell type in which Ppargc1b showed its strongest sub-FDR TCA/OXPHOS tail.

story_title: SRRM2 and several RNA-processing perturbations expose recurrent but nonidentical nuclear-speckle transcript responses
proxy_summary: A restricted 151 signature-neighbor screen linked the Nop56 response to Uba5, Rrn3, Ufc1, Ufsp2, Eif4e, and Rbm28 and inversely to Slc17a5, Nefl, and Foxg1.
proxy_why_it_matters: These neighbors nominate a broader nucleolar-translation/proteostasis network for follow-up and show that inverse signatures were not merely canonical Nop56 complex members with opposite effects.

story_title: GRIN2B and DLGAP4 perturbations independently lower Vgf in cortical projection neurons
proxy_summary: Grin2b and Grin2a were not interchangeable in L2/3 IT cortical cells; their signatures were anticorrelated and their FDR genes did not overlap.
proxy_why_it_matters: Even closely related GluN2 subunits within the same receptor family drove opposite activity-gene behavior in the same cell class, emphasizing subunit-specific downstream wiring.

story_title: TSC2 perturbation induces a cerebellar GABA synaptic and calcium-transcript state
proxy_summary: Tsc1 was the nearest positive non-self Tsc2 neighbor in the main responsive classes, while Mtor and Rptor were inverse neighbors in 155 MB Glut and Mtor was the most anti-correlated perturbation in three responsive classes.
proxy_why_it_matters: The convergence with another TSC-complex subunit and opposition to the downstream kinase node verify the expected TSC-to-mTORC1 directionality at whole-transcriptome scale.

story_title: KMT2B perturbation produces a mostly repressive thalamic neuronal state with a smaller midbrain core
proxy_summary: A small negative marker panel recurred across Kmt2b-responsive cell types, with Stxbp2 and Csf2ra as the most replicated FDR-supported genes.
proxy_why_it_matters: These genes provide practical readouts for candidate Kmt2b activity even though the module is not a recognizable curated pathway.

story_title: VPS35 perturbation remodels a thalamic synaptic-receptor and excitability transcript set
proxy_summary: In the 151 TH Prkcd cell type, Rab7 was a modest top positive Vps35 signature neighbor, whereas Ap2s1 and Ap2m1 were among the strongest negative neighbors.
proxy_why_it_matters: This restricted comparison recovers a known Rab7-retromer connection while also suggesting that loss of the AP-2 endocytic adaptor subunits pushes this neuronal state away from the Vps35-loss program.

story_title: GRIN1 perturbation induces a broad thalamic growth-factor and synaptic-remodeling state
proxy_summary: Restricted-signature neighbor analysis linked the 151 Grin1 program to Vps54, Atp6v0c, Scn1b, Snap25, and Dlgap4 while identifying Wdfy3, Gabrb2, and Gsk3b as opposing signatures.
proxy_why_it_matters: The nearest signatures were not other NMDA receptor subunits, reinforcing that the downstream Grin1 state is a broader cellular response that can converge with non-receptor perturbations.

story_title: CELF2 perturbation collapses a thalamic CELF-family state and recurrently induces Snhg11
proxy_summary: Other neuronal RNA-binding or RNA-processing perturbations are not interchangeable with Celf2, and the closest global Celf2 signature neighbors are only modestly correlated.
proxy_why_it_matters: The contrast prevents over-generalizing all splicing-factor perturbations into a single neuronal RBP state: Rbfox1, Fmr1, Adar, Adarb1, Hnrnpu, and Srsf1 did not recapitulate Celf2, while the strongest 151 neighbors such as Cic, Dctn1, Dync1h1, and Tsc2 had r values of only 0.20-0.26.

story_title: ZC3H14 perturbation recurrently induces Zcchc18 while lowering polyadenylation-factor transcripts
proxy_summary: The two strongest glutamatergic responses converged on nuclear RNA-processing factors, especially Pabpn1 down-regulation in both 151 TH and 155 MB Glut and Cstf2 down-regulation in 155 MB Glut.
proxy_why_it_matters: Pabpn1 and Cstf2 are biologically close to ZC3H14's poly(A)/mRNA 3-prime processing biology, turning a short gene list into a plausible RNA-metabolism response rather than an arbitrary stress signature.

story_title: QRICH1 perturbation recurrently lowers a Scn2b-Celf3-Ldhd module in thalamic and caudal neurons
proxy_summary: A recurrent Qrich1 module centered on Scn2b, Celf3, Ldhd, and Tlcd3b was repeatedly downregulated across responsive neuronal classes.
proxy_why_it_matters: The repeated gene-level direction across independent cell-class tests argues that the phenotype is not driven solely by one thalamic outlier and nominates Scn2b/Celf3/Ldhd/Tlcd3b as better downstream readouts than the weak Qrich1 mRNA row.

story_title: MARCHF6 and TXNDC15 perturbations converge on a narrow neuronal SREBP2 sterol-feedback module
proxy_summary: The 155 MB Glut Txndc15 sterol module follows Marchf6-loss direction and opposes Srebf2-loss direction, but this coupling is absent in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
proxy_why_it_matters: This places the Txndc15 response near ER cholesterol-control biology while showing that pathway competence is not enough: the same cell type can respond to Marchf6 and Srebf2 perturbation but ignore Txndc15 loss at the transcriptome level.

story_title: XPO1 targeting produces an RNA-gain state with Arrdc3-Slc16a6 induction and RNA-processing repression
proxy_summary: Snrnp70 and Srsf1 perturbations aligned positively with Xpo1 signatures even though endogenous Snrnp70 and Srsf-family transcripts were repressed by Xpo1 targeting.
proxy_why_it_matters: The negative RBP transcripts are unlikely to be a simple linear loss-of-Snrnp70 driver; both gain of Xpo1 and gain of selected splicing-factor targets can lead cells toward a shared RNA-processing stress state.

story_title: NALCN perturbation lowers a compact Opn3-Slc6a17-Tspan33 module in thalamic neurons
proxy_summary: Nalcn-loss signatures are weakly correlated with GPCR regulators and with several efficiently knocked down neuronal ion-channel perturbations.
proxy_why_it_matters: The result argues that chronic loss of the NALCN pore has a transcriptomic consequence distinct from muscarinic/tachykinin/neurotensin receptor knockdown and from voltage-gated Na+/K+/HCN-channel depletion.

story_title: ATXN1 and CIC perturbations converge almost perfectly on a thalamic mixed-direction state
proxy_summary: The ATXN1 complex member is the strongest positive signature neighbor of Cic, specifically in TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons.
proxy_why_it_matters: ATXN1 is a physical and functional CIC partner, so this convergence supports the biological specificity of the TH signature and extends ATXN1-CIC complex activity to a thalamic neuronal subclass.

story_title: GFPT1 perturbation couples Ogt repression to ER and integrated-stress induction
proxy_summary: Direct Ogt perturbation is not transcriptionally interchangeable with Gfpt1 perturbation, even though Ogt is strongly downregulated inside the Gfpt1 signature.
proxy_why_it_matters: The Gfpt1 phenotype is unlikely to be explained by a simple linear GFPT1-to-OGT mRNA axis; HBP loss may stress neurons through N-glycosylation or other UDP-GlcNAc-dependent processes as well as O-GlcNAcylation.

story_title: TUBA1A perturbation induces asymmetric beta-tubulin and TUBA4A compensation
proxy_summary: Tuba1a depletion triggers a tubulin-isotype compensation program in a restricted pair of neuronal classes.
proxy_why_it_matters: Alpha- and beta-tubulins function as heterodimers, so a cell that lowers Tuba1a while increasing Tuba4a and multiple beta-tubulin genes is changing the stoichiometry of the microtubule building-block pool rather than mounting a generic stress response.

story_title: CHD8 perturbation produces a recurrent caudal Pnisr-Usp11-Dus3l repression state
proxy_summary: Chd8 signatures were not interchangeable with several direct CHD8 interactors or chromatin-disease neighbors; Ctnnb1, Chd7, Ctcf, Setd1a, Chd4, Smarce1, and Kansl1 were weakly correlated or anticorrelated while Yy1 and Ppp2r1a were only modest positive neighbors.
proxy_why_it_matters: The relation between disease chromatin regulators depends on cell type and network position; direct physical proximity to CHD8 did not predict a matching perturbation state.

story_title: ATP1A3 perturbation induces ion-pump and synaptic remodeling distinct from ATP2A2 ER stress
proxy_summary: The thalamic Atp1a3 program was not reproduced by the related Na,K-ATPase alpha perturbations Atp1a1 or Atp1a2.
proxy_why_it_matters: This supports alpha-3 being functionally nonredundant in neurons co-expressing alpha-1, and it prevents treating all Na,K-ATPase alpha subunits as interchangeable in Perturb-seq interpretation.

story_title: KMT2A perturbation reveals a mature thalamic Nr2f1-Pcdh7-Lhx9 maintenance state
proxy_summary: Kmt2a did not phenocopy other H3K4/chromatin perturbations; Kmt2d was the strongest negative signature neighbor in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
proxy_why_it_matters: Even paralogous or physically connected chromatin regulators were not interchangeable in this neuronal state, so shared chromatin neighborhoods were a poor predictor of acute regulon direction.

story_title: YLPM1 perturbation lowers Srsf6-Srsf5 and Inha in midbrain-linked neurons
proxy_summary: The 155 MB Glut downstream signature converged on nuclear body and nuclear speck genes, including downregulation of the splicing factors Srsf6 and Srsf5.
proxy_why_it_matters: This connects the strongest Ylpm1 phenotype to a plausible nuclear RNA-processing compartment rather than to a generic activity or stress response.

story_title: BMAL1-CLOCK and REV-ERB perturbations recover an asymmetric neuronal circadian feedback loop
proxy_summary: The thalamic Nr1d2 response is a weak subset of the Nr1d1 perturbation program.
proxy_why_it_matters: Paralog convergence extends beyond the marker Nr1d1 itself and suggests that TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons expose a REV-ERB-sensitive gene module.

story_title: HSPA8 perturbation induces a compact HSP70-HSP90 compensatory transcript arm
proxy_summary: Hspa8 is not transcriptionally interchangeable with Hsp90ab1, Hspd1, or targeted DnaJ co-chaperones.
proxy_why_it_matters: The related-target comparison preserves a negative result: components of the chaperone web share interactors but produce distinguishable perturbation states, with only partial similarity to Hspa9 and Hspa5.

story_title: PPP3CA and PPP3R1 perturbations expose a noncanonical calcineurin transcript output opposite AP-2 adaptor states
proxy_summary: AP-2 adaptor perturbations formed the strongest anticorrelated signature neighbors of Ppp3r1 in the thalamic class.
proxy_why_it_matters: The reversal of multiple Ppp3r1-regulated 151 genes by Ap2s1 and Ap2m1 suggests an antagonistic transcriptional relationship between PPP3R1-dependent calcium phosphatase signaling and clathrin-adaptor endocytic perturbations, a hypothesis consistent with—but more specific than—the known role of calcineurin in synaptic vesicle endocytosis.

story_title: ACTB perturbation recurrently induces ACTG1 and FLNA without reciprocal ACTG1 compensation
proxy_summary: Cfl2, Cdc42, Cyfip2, Cyfip1, Rac1, and Limk1 perturbations did not reveal a shared ACTG1-like actin transcriptomic module.
proxy_why_it_matters: A curated actin-network connection does not imply that partially silencing individual actin regulators in these neurons will drive a common RNA phenotype.

story_title: CAML perturbation lowers receptor, ion-pump, and synaptic-vesicle transcripts
proxy_summary: Caml signatures weakly but recurrently resembled V-ATPase, clathrin/vesicle, and proteasome perturbations more than they showed any strong opposite neighbor.
proxy_why_it_matters: Direct WRB/ASNA1/GET-family comparisons were not available in the perturbation panel, but the nearest positive neighbors point to organelle acidification, vesicle traffic, and protein turnover machinery as transcriptomic neighbors of CAML loss in neurons.

story_title: SRSF1 perturbation rewires splice-regulator abundance instead of inducing SRSF2 compensation
proxy_summary: Srsf1 depletion did not induce a simple compensatory increase of the related SR factor Srsf2 or its CLK regulators; Srsf2, Hnrnpdl, Clk4 and Clk1 were recurrently reduced.
proxy_why_it_matters: This converts the response from an intuitive one-factor knockdown into a collapse of part of the SR-protein regulatory network, which could amplify functional consequences of Srsf1 dosage loss.

story_title: HSF1 perturbation lowers a basal HSPH1-HSP90 support module
proxy_summary: Hsf1 perturbation did not produce FDR-level regulation of Hspa5, Hspa9, or Hspd1.
proxy_why_it_matters: The most reproducible signal stayed within the Hsph1/Hsp90 branch rather than collapsing all measured chaperone systems, a useful negative result for annotating the perturbation as a selective basal HSF1 output.

story_title: CTCF perturbation robustly represses clustered protocadherins in thalamic and midbrain neurons
proxy_summary: Perturbing cohesin-axis genes, Yy1, Chd7, or Chd8 did not reproduce the Ctcf Zcwpw2/Dennd6b/Abhd14b module in the strongest Ctcf cell types.
proxy_why_it_matters: CTCF-associated architectural machinery is not interchangeable at these neuronal loci: the Ctcf phenotype appears anchor- or locus-specific rather than a generic consequence of perturbing any chromatin-loop regulator.

story_title: APC, CTNNB1, and TCF7L2 perturbations recover opposing Wnt-node polarity with neuronal-state outputs
proxy_summary: Ctnnb1 loss opposed Apc perturbation on the Wnt-feedback program in the same 151 thalamic class.
proxy_why_it_matters: This reciprocal direction is the expected topology for an inhibitory destruction-complex component versus the beta-catenin transcriptional effector, and it validates Axin2 and Notum as directional readouts of the local Wnt response.

story_title: PTEN perturbation recovers the expected TSC–mTOR polarity while remodeling neuronal AKT and mitochondrial transcripts
proxy_summary: Tsc1 was the nearest positive non-self Tsc2 neighbor in the main responsive classes, while Mtor and Rptor were inverse neighbors in 155 MB Glut and Mtor was the most anti-correlated perturbation in three responsive classes.
proxy_why_it_matters: The convergence with another TSC-complex subunit and opposition to the downstream kinase node verify the expected TSC-to-mTORC1 directionality at whole-transcriptome scale.

story_title: MYEF2 perturbation repeatedly induces a DZIP3–VBP1–IST1 marker triad in subcortical neurons
proxy_summary: Pura knockdown did not phenocopy Myef2 knockdown in the strongest Myef2-responsive classes even though PURA is a reported antagonist of MyEF2 binding at the Mbp MB1 promoter.
proxy_why_it_matters: The Dzip3/Vbp1/Ist1 output is unlikely to be a simple readout of the canonical PURA–MyEF2–MB1 promoter switch described for Mbp regulation.

story_title: ANKRD11 and SETD5 perturbations converge on a thalamic synaptic-receptor marker module
proxy_summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Ankrd11 signature converged with Setd5 but was orthogonal to Ankrd12 and inverted by Med23/Wdr26 on the same restricted gene set.
proxy_why_it_matters: This links two haploinsufficient neurodevelopmental chromatin genes at the signature level while warning that ankyrin-repeat name similarity or generic transcriptional cofactor status does not predict phenocopying.

story_title: MIB1 perturbation induces a recurrent neuronal sterol response that tested Notch perturbations do not reproduce
proxy_summary: Dll1 had no coherent positive or inverse signature neighbor among Notch1-4 receptors or among all assayed perturbations.
proxy_why_it_matters: Although DLL1 is placed upstream of multiple Notch receptors, the single-cell RNA signatures do not show receptor-like convergence that would support a shared autonomous state transition.

story_title: KANSL1 perturbation recurrently represses an endolysosomal-associated posterior neuronal module
proxy_summary: Genome-wide score correlations placed Bap1, Setd1a, and Kmt5b among the closest positive neighbors and Trrap, Wdr26, Phf12, and Sin3a among the closest negative neighbors in 155 MB Glut, but all absolute correlations were modest.
proxy_why_it_matters: The result preserves a weak but biologically pointed signature-neighbor signal while showing that no neighboring perturbation captured a strong Kansl1-like state.

story_title: BPTF and CHD4 perturbations drive opposite directions on a diagnostic posterior-neuronal marker set
proxy_summary: The Bptf signature diverged from Chd4, another chromatin-remodeling perturbation, with Chd4 scoring as the strongest restricted negative neighbor in both 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
proxy_why_it_matters: The result argues against collapsing chromatin remodelers into one expected transcriptomic direction: NURF-linked Bptf and NuRD-linked Chd4 can drive opposing expression on the genes most diagnostic of Bptf perturbation.

story_title: THAP11 and THAP1 perturbations produce non-interchangeable subcortical transcriptional states
proxy_summary: Ogt was the top positive restricted-signature neighbor of Thap11 on the 20-gene core, especially sharing the down-regulated arm in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
proxy_why_it_matters: The convergence is mechanistically plausible because OGT processes HCF-1 and HCF-1 is used by THAP11/ZNF143 complexes, suggesting partial convergence on an HCF-1-linked chromatin axis.

story_title: GATAD1 and PHF12 perturbations share a sparse organelle/RNA-processing output not reproduced by nearby chromatin regulators
proxy_summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the induced spliceosome/RNP program was coupled to repression of synaptic, glutamatergic and neuronal-projection genes such as Gls, Syt7, Grin2c, Snap25 and Tubb3.
proxy_why_it_matters: A PHF12 loss-like perturbation can downshift neuronal effector genes while upshifting RNA-processing genes, so the response cannot be summarized as simple de-repression by loss of a transcriptional repressor.

story_title: ATRX and CHD8 perturbations move CSF2RA in opposite directions in the same thalamic and midbrain neurons
proxy_summary: Chd8 signatures were not interchangeable with several direct CHD8 interactors or chromatin-disease neighbors; Ctnnb1, Chd7, Ctcf, Setd1a, Chd4, Smarce1, and Kansl1 were weakly correlated or anticorrelated while Yy1 and Ppp2r1a were only modest positive neighbors.
proxy_why_it_matters: The relation between disease chromatin regulators depends on cell type and network position; direct physical proximity to CHD8 did not predict a matching perturbation state.

story_title: DEAF1 perturbation reproducibly lowers an EIF4G3–RAC3–B4GAT1–TMEM80 module
proxy_summary: Deaf1 perturbation reproducibly decreased an Eif4g3/Rac3/B4gat1/Tmem80 module in thalamic, midbrain, hindbrain, and one cortical glutamatergic class.
proxy_why_it_matters: The dominant signal is not a broad collapse of the Deaf1 transcript; it is a compact, recurrent downstream module that can be followed as candidate DEAF1-output genes in neurons.

story_title: PRDM10 perturbation repeatedly represses a MADD–CADM3–PTOV1 neuronal module
proxy_summary: The active Prdm10 signatures converged on a recurrent down-regulated module led by Madd, Cadm3, and Ptov1.
proxy_why_it_matters: The repeated ordering of these genes across unrelated neuronal classes argues for a core PRDM10-dependent state rather than entirely idiosyncratic cell-type responses.

story_title: CHD2 perturbation couples RNA-processing and ion-channel repression without phenocopying other CHD remodelers
proxy_summary: Within the main 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response, Chd2 perturbation downregulated RNA-splicing components and several potassium/ion-channel transcripts.
proxy_why_it_matters: The affected genes nominate RNA processing and neuronal excitability effectors as nearby transcriptomic outputs of Chd2 disruption rather than merely confirming a generic chromatin-remodeling label.

story_title: Cytosolic MDH1 and GOT1 perturbations separate from mitochondrial malate–aspartate-shuttle components
proxy_summary: Mdh1, the cytosolic malate dehydrogenase partner of Got1, was the closest positive Got1 signature neighbor in the principal responsive thalamic class.
proxy_why_it_matters: This links the Got1 phenotype to the cytosolic half of the malate-aspartate shuttle rather than to an arbitrary amino-transferase effect.

story_title: NatB and NatA perturbations produce separable neuronal states rather than a common acetyltransferase response
proxy_summary: NatB/Naa20 does not phenocopy the available NatA perturbations.
proxy_why_it_matters: Although NAA20, NAA10, and NAA15 all belong to the N-terminal acetyltransferase family, Naa10 produced no FDR-significant genes and Naa15 signatures were weaker and essentially uncorrelated with Naa20, supporting NatB-specific neuronal biology rather than interchangeability among NAT complexes.

story_title: SLC7A6OS perturbation couples POLR2A induction to partial nuclear-speckle transcript repression
proxy_summary: Responsive Slc7a6os strata up-regulate Polr2a and Son while repressing Srrm2 and Pnisr, suggesting mixed compensation to Pol-II/RNA-processing stress.
proxy_why_it_matters: The direction is not simple Pol-II transcript loss; it points to a compensatory nuclear RNA-processing state after Slc7a6os perturbation.

story_title: ZBTB7A perturbation produces a broad neuronal state with little overlap to ZBTB18
proxy_summary: Zbtb7a did not phenocopy other assayed Zbtb-family or NuRD-associated perturbations; Gatad2b and Chd4 were only modestly positive neighbors, whereas Yy1, Huwe1, Trrap, and Chd8 were recurrent inverse neighbors.
proxy_why_it_matters: Known corepressor relationships are insufficient to predict the neuronal Zbtb7a state; the dataset instead points to a context-specific chromatin-regulatory balance.

story_title: SETD1A perturbation links recurrent organelle-gene repression to a modest TSC-associated signature neighborhood
proxy_summary: The strongest MB Glut signature contained an up-regulated RNA-processing branch, with Pnn, Srsf2, Srsf6, Srsf7, Srrm2, Ddx41, Dhx16, and Brd9 increased while most FDR genes decreased.
proxy_why_it_matters: Separating the minority positive branch from the dominant negative module suggests that some nuclear RNA-processing genes may be secondarily induced rather than directly lost after SETD1A reduction.

story_title: USP48 perturbation induces a compact ABHD12B–RESP18 state while repressing CYP46A1
proxy_summary: A restricted 38-gene Usp48 tail aligned with Kdm4c, Adnp, and Chd4 and opposed Trip12 and Arid2.
proxy_why_it_matters: This connects the most perturbed Usp48 genes to chromatin-regulator perturbations and an opposing ubiquitin-ligase neighbor, suggesting a follow-up hypothesis beyond the annotated TRAF2/NF-kappaB function.

story_title: POLR3B and BDP1 perturbations split into Rap/adhesion and tRNA-stress states
proxy_summary: The Pol III pathway neighbor Bdp1 was not interchangeable with Polr3b in 151 TH neurons: Bdp1 induced Ddit3 and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase genes, whereas Polr3b induced the Rap/adhesion program, and the two FDR<0.05 hit lists did not overlap.
proxy_why_it_matters: A shared Pol III annotation would predict related transcriptional consequences; the data separate a TFIIIB/initiation-factor stress response from the RPC2/core-subunit neuronal response.

story_title: SKI perturbation reveals a mature cortical marker state rather than a canonical SMAD response
proxy_summary: Ski knockdown did not resolve into a canonical SMAD/TGF-beta/BMP transcriptional program in the responsive neuronal classes.
proxy_why_it_matters: SKI is curated as a SMAD-binding TGF-beta/BMP corepressor, so the absence of adjusted Smad7/Id/Junb/Serpine1 induction and the weak correlations to receptor, SMAD, and corepressor perturbations indicate cell-state or threshold gating of the canonical pathway.

story_title: Acute HNRNPH2 perturbation links RSRP1 repression to TCA-gene induction without paralog compensation
proxy_summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Hnrnph2 signature coupled Rsrp1 loss to induction of the TCA-cycle genes Idh3g and Ogdh.
proxy_why_it_matters: HNRNPH2 is annotated as an RNA-processing factor, so coordinated positive scores for two mitochondrial TCA components create an unexpected metabolism-linked branch of the loss-of-Hnrnph2 response.

story_title: DDX3X perturbation separates a thalamic NMDA/junctional state from a midbrain trafficking state
proxy_summary: A nominal recurrent module, especially Bicd2 induction and Ddx5 induction, appeared in several posterior or GABAergic classes even when per-class FDR was weak.
proxy_why_it_matters: Ddx5 is a STRING functional partner of DDX3X, so recurrent Ddx5 up-regulation is a plausible but exploratory RNA-helicase compensation marker; Bicd2 was the most recurrent nominal positive gene and may mark a broader Ddx3x-stress response.

story_title: CTBP1 and ZEB1 perturbations share a trafficking cassette that ZEB2 does not reproduce
proxy_summary: The principal Zeb1 downstream program was a compact AP1M2/STXBP2/PATJ/SPINT2/F11R/CDC42BPG cassette rather than a broad canonical EMT signature.
proxy_why_it_matters: The module direction matches the idea that Zeb1 suppresses polarity and epithelial-like genes, but its narrow size and composition argue for a specialized neuronal regulon.

story_title: GTF2I and GTF2IRD1 perturbations produce distinct neuronal outputs within the Williams–Beuren interval
proxy_summary: Gtf2ird1 was transcriptomically divergent from Gtf2i, Baz1b, Clip2, and Limk1 in the thalamic class despite their Williams-Beuren and STRING proximity.
proxy_why_it_matters: The result argues that 7q11.23/WBS genes should not be treated as interchangeable perturbations in this cell type.

story_title: CHD4 perturbation raises ion-channel genes while repressing a beta-protocadherin cassette
proxy_summary: Several BAF/PBAF chromatin-remodeler perturbations were among the strongest Chd4-opposed signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
proxy_why_it_matters: Closely related chromatin-disease genes can point in opposite transcriptomic directions in the same neuronal class; downstream readouts from a NuRD perturbation should not be assumed to phenocopy BAF-family loss.

story_title: MED15, MED13, and MED23 perturbations converge on repression of a thalamic synaptic module
proxy_summary: Within the thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c cell class, Med23 converged with Med15 and Med13 on the same downregulated neuronal module but diverged from Cdk8 and Med12.
proxy_why_it_matters: The result argues that physical membership in Mediator is not sufficient to predict an interchangeable Perturb-seq phenotype in this neuronal state.

story_title: MYT1L and PHF21A perturbations converge narrowly on RREB1 induction
proxy_summary: Sin3a and Phf21a drive opposite Rreb1 directions in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut despite both belonging to HDAC1/2-associated chromatin-repressor biology.
proxy_why_it_matters: The directionality of Rreb1 is complex-specific: shared access to HDAC1/2 does not predict the same transcriptional state, warning against treating deacetylase-core perturbations as interchangeable.

story_title: DHX9, TPR, and TNPO3 perturbations define overlapping but non-identical nuclear RNP and pore-basket states
proxy_summary: The engaged L5 ET response couples Ranbp2 depletion to RNA-processing and SUMO/nuclear-protein genes.
proxy_why_it_matters: The L5 ET gene set is the cleanest in-dataset bridge between measured Ranbp2 knockdown and the known RANBP2 SUMO E3/nuclear-envelope mechanism.

story_title: AHDC1 perturbation represses a neuronal surface and synaptic cassette without canonical Wnt activation
proxy_summary: Ahdc1 had no robust all-gene signature neighbor among the 151 TH perturbations.
proxy_why_it_matters: The response did not recapitulate the tested chromatin, Wnt, or neurodevelopmental perturbations; even the strongest Ahdc1 correlations were near zero and one safe-target control appeared among the nearest positives.

story_title: VEZF1 perturbation produces a compact HR–PRKCG–RASA4-down and TLE2–ABI2-up neuronal state
proxy_summary: Ctcf and Dnmt3a perturbations did not recapitulate the Vezf1 thalamic signature, while Zbtb7a showed a weak inverse restricted signature.
proxy_why_it_matters: This preserves a mechanistically important non-equivalence among chromatin and zinc-finger perturbations: Vezf1 output cannot be treated as generic CTCF-barrier or de novo DNA-methylation loss in this thalamic context.

story_title: CACNA1G perturbation produces a thalamic RNA state not reproduced by other calcium-channel perturbations
proxy_summary: The 151 thalamic Cacna1g program was not reproduced by other calcium-channel or calcium-dependent perturbations.
proxy_why_it_matters: Even in the cell type where several calcium-pathway targets were measurably knocked down, Cacna1g behaved as a specific Cav3.1 node rather than a generic voltage-gated-calcium or calcineurin signature.

story_title: Zbtb18 perturbation induces an Endou-Pxdn-Clstn2-Man2a2 module in thalamic neurons
proxy_summary: Candidate Zbtb18 co-repressor perturbations Dnmt3a and Ctbp1 did not reproduce the Zbtb18 Endou/Pxdn/Clstn2/Man2a2 thalamic program.
proxy_why_it_matters: Physical or functional association with a sequence-specific repressor is not enough to make a perturbation a transcriptomic proxy for Zbtb18; this also cautions against using broad chromatin-corepressor modulation as a Zbtb18-directed therapeutic proxy.

story_title: CUL3 perturbation lowers a compact RNA-processing module without a KLHL7 phenocopy
proxy_summary: The two Cul3-responsive glutamatergic classes shared a small down-regulated nuclear RNA-processing module anchored by Pnisr, Rsrp1, Snhg11 and Srsf5.
proxy_why_it_matters: This recurring module is not the canonical NRF2 output of CUL3 biology and generates a hypothesis that Cul3 loss perturbs spliceosome or nuclear-speckle regulation in selected neurons.

story_title: Creb1 perturbation recurrently induces Crem without recreating an activity-induced CREB program
proxy_summary: Crem induction is specific to Creb1 perturbation rather than a generic consequence of disrupting upstream cAMP, NMDA-receptor, or CaMKII inputs.
proxy_why_it_matters: Although PKA, Ca2+/CaMK, and glutamatergic signaling converge on CREB phosphorylation, efficient Prkaca, Camk2b, Grin2b, Grin2a, and Adcy3 perturbations did not recreate the Creb1-to-Crem signature in the same classes, arguing that the signal is a CREB-family identity or compensation response rather than simple loss of upstream drive.

story_title: KCC2 perturbation evokes an immediate-early response in thalamic Prkcd-Grin2c neurons
proxy_summary: Slc12a5 was not phenocopied by strongly engaged Gabra1, Gabrg2, Kcnq2, or Kcnq3 perturbations in the same thalamic glutamatergic class.
proxy_why_it_matters: This contrast argues that the Fos/Nr4a1/Dusp1 program is not a generic consequence of successful receptor or ion-channel knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; KCC2 loss occupies a narrower chloride-homeostasis axis that couples to IEGs in this assay.

story_title: Manf perturbation recurrently induces an Hspa5-centered ER-chaperone response
proxy_summary: In the strongest MB Glut context, the positive Manf signature neighborhood was enriched for perturbations of ER/secretory/UPS-adjacent genes such as Gfpt1, Dhdds, Sec31a, Atp2a2, Pomp, Psmb4, Psmc1, Psmc5, and Hspa5, whereas no strong anti-correlated neighbor appeared.
proxy_why_it_matters: This links Manf loss to a broader proteostasis liability network rather than to a single linear UPR transcription factor.

story_title: Pde10a perturbation produces a narrow Scg2-positive state in striatal-lineage GABA neurons
proxy_summary: The isolated Ubac2 signal in 308 CB GABA is disconnected from the target-engaged striatal Pde10a signature.
proxy_why_it_matters: It prevents overinterpretation of a single cerebellar FDR hit as PDE10A/cAMP biology when the target transcript itself was not significantly reduced.

story_title: Atp2a2 and Elp2 perturbations converge on an amino-acid and ER-stress state
proxy_summary: The Atp2a2 151 signature aligned more with stress/proteostasis neighbors than with the available Ryr, Itpr, Stim, or Atf6 calcium-pathway perturbations.
proxy_why_it_matters: This argues that the measured Atp2a2 state is not just a generic ER-calcium-homeostasis perturbation captured by other channels or sensors; however, the top-neighbor analysis also exposes that several high correlations lack clean target-transcript knockdown.

story_title: Rora perturbation represses a thalamic excitability and synaptic-output state
proxy_summary: Rora, but not Rorb or Rorc, drove a strong ROR-family signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
proxy_why_it_matters: The contrast argues that ROR paralogs are not interchangeable in this in vivo neuronal screen even though curated pathways connect them to the same RORE logic.

story_title: Wac perturbation couples loss of mature neuronal effectors to increased RNA-processing transcripts
proxy_summary: The strongest Wac response paired loss of synaptic genes with increased nuclear speckle, splicing, and ubiquitin-linked transcripts such as Luc7l2, Luc7l3, Sf3b1, Rbm25, Rbm4, Srsf11, Clk1, Jmjd1c, and Ube2b.
proxy_why_it_matters: This suggests that Wac-deficient neurons activate a nuclear RNA-processing or chromatin compensation program rather than simply reducing all transcription.

story_title: Vps37a perturbation increases V-ATPase transcripts while reducing synaptic membrane genes
proxy_summary: The most recurrent positive module after Vps37a perturbation is lysosomal/vacuolar acidification, centered on Atp6v1h and Atp6v0b.
proxy_why_it_matters: Induction of V-ATPase and lysosomal membrane genes is directionally coherent with impaired ESCRT-dependent delivery of cargo to lysosomes and nominates an acidification response as a readout of Vps37a disruption.

story_title: Autophagy-initiation perturbations reduce ER and endomembrane transcripts in selected neuronal states
proxy_summary: In 155 MB Glut, the top Atg5-ranked genes locally resembled Rb1cc1, Atg16l1, and proteasome perturbations but not Map1lc3a or Sqstm1.
proxy_why_it_matters: The result separates Atg5-proximal or proteostasis-neighbor signatures from downstream LC3/p62 perturbations, arguing that autophagy-related perturbations are not interchangeable in this assay.

story_title: Atp2b1 loss induces a thalamic activity-like state not shared by PMCA2 or PMCA3 loss
proxy_summary: Atp2b2 and Atp2b3 knockdowns did not phenocopy Atp2b1 in the Atp2b1-responsive thalamic class.
proxy_why_it_matters: The result argues that PMCA paralogs are not functionally interchangeable in this single-cell transcriptional assay, even when Atp2b2 and Atp2b3 target transcripts are efficiently reduced.

story_title: Mecp2 perturbation yields sparse, context-dependent excitability and membrane-gene changes
proxy_summary: A neuronal excitability/membrane module was altered in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with Cacna1g down-regulation recurring in 155 MB Glut.
proxy_why_it_matters: This separates a small, reproducible downstream signal from the many one-off cell-type hits and nominates Cacna1g as a directionally consistent marker of Mecp2 loss in glutamatergic thalamic/midbrain-like classes.

story_title: Eif4e suppression induces an Rnpc3-Amy1-high, Rsrp1-low abundance state
proxy_summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Eif4e depletion coincided with increased Eif4a2, Eif4g2, Eif3l, Eif3f, Eif5, Eef1a1 and HSP90/proteasome-associated genes.
proxy_why_it_matters: The signature is compatible with compensatory rebuilding of translation-initiation and protein-quality-control capacity downstream of reduced cap-binding EIF4E.

story_title: Cltc loss couples Jun-Stmn4 stress induction to loss of synaptic membrane transcripts
proxy_summary: Top positive Cltc signature neighbors were repeatedly Vps, Atp6, Psm/Psmc and Sec31a perturbations, whereas AP-2, dynamin and Synj1 neighbors mostly failed to rank with the top Cltc-like signatures.
proxy_why_it_matters: CLTC is physically and functionally tied to AP-2, so the restricted-signature result suggests that the Cltc RNA state is closer to broader endomembrane/proteostasis perturbations than to knockdown of every canonical endocytic partner.

story_title: Ntrk2 loss lowers a Vgf-Atp2a2 branch in thalamic neurons and Akap5 in Pvalb neurons
proxy_summary: In thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells, the Ntrk2-loss signature was weakly opposite to Nf1 and Pten perturbations while Atp2a2 and Vgf were the FDR-level downstream Ntrk2 outputs.
proxy_why_it_matters: NTRK2 activates RAS and PI3K signaling whereas NF1 and PTEN are pathway brakes, so the weak anti-correlation is directionally consistent with receptor loss being transcriptionally opposed to removal of some downstream negative regulators.

story_title: TBL1XR1 and GSK3B perturbations do not collapse onto a canonical beta-catenin state
proxy_summary: The Tbl1xr1 thalamic signature was weakly correlated with Ctnnb1, Tcf7l2, and Tbl1x perturbations despite known TBL1XR1 links to TBL1X and β-catenin.
proxy_why_it_matters: Related-target divergence argues against reading the Tbl1xr1 result as a simple β-catenin or TBL1X paralog phenotype.

story_title: Thra loss represses Hr and Adgrb1 in thalamic Prkcd-Grin2c neurons
proxy_summary: Thrb, Rxra, Rxrb, Rxrg, Ncoa1, and Ncoa3 did not phenocopy Thra in the two cell types where Thra was most evident.
proxy_why_it_matters: Although these genes encode a paralog, RXR partners, or nuclear-receptor coactivators, the dataset did not show an interchangeable receptor-complex signature at FDR scale.

story_title: Kcnb1 perturbation raises a Bdnf-Vgf-Scg2-Nptx2 module in L4-5 IT neurons
proxy_summary: Restricted-signature neighbors split L4/5 comparator perturbations into Kcnb1-like and Kcnb1-opposing groups.
proxy_why_it_matters: Kcnb1 was positively aligned with Grin2a, Arhgef9, Gabrb3, Kcnq2, Gabrg2 and Scn2a, but opposed to Grin2b, Ank3, Syngap1, Shank2, Camk2a and Kcnd3, so the named perturbations should not be collapsed into a single direction of transcriptomic effect.

story_title: Atxn10 and Eef1a2 perturbations share selected synaptic and cytoskeletal liabilities without broad phenocopy
proxy_summary: The recurrent signature-neighbor clue linking Atxn10 to Gfpt1-targeted perturbations is directionally compatible with the ATXN10-OGT literature, while the stronger Pvalb neighbors point to V-ATPase, VCP, proteasome, and mitochondrial-chaperone perturbation states.
proxy_why_it_matters: This prioritizes O-GlcNAc/hexosamine biology for mechanistic follow-up without ignoring that the strongest dataset similarities are broader proteostasis or organelle-homeostasis signatures.

story_title: Spliceosome and TREX perturbations repeatedly generate posterior RNA-processing abundance states
proxy_summary: Direct Rnpc3 complex-member perturbations were absent, but a restricted Rnpc3-module screen found convergence with Srsf1, Prpf6, Ddx23 and U2af2 and opposition to Cdk13, Trrap, Ppp2r1a and Yy1.
proxy_why_it_matters: The Rnpc3 module is not unique to the minor spliceosome; it aligns with some major spliceosome/RNA-processing perturbations but reverses under other nuclear regulators, making the module a context-specific stress signature rather than a generic RNA-processing readout.

story_title: Multiple mitochondrial-maintenance perturbations converge on an amino-acid stress state
proxy_summary: Dnm1l unexpectedly phenocopied Opa1 transcriptional stress signatures, whereas several other OPA1 interactors or mitochondrial-dynamics neighbors did not.
proxy_why_it_matters: OPA1 and DRP1/DNM1L sit on opposite sides of the fusion-fission morphology balance, yet perturbing either GTPase produced co-oriented Opa1-like amino-acid signatures in multiple sensitive cell types. The data therefore point to shared mitochondrial distress as the transcriptomic endpoint, not a simple sign reversal between fusion and fission genes.

story_title: Dhdds perturbation induces ER and amino-acid stress while reducing neuronal effector transcripts
proxy_summary: Dhdds signatures were positively related to perturbations of Gfpt1, Hspa9, Atp2a2, Hspa5, proteasome, and ER trafficking genes, while opposing full-transcriptome neighbors were weak.
proxy_why_it_matters: The sensitive-cell Dhdds state sits inside a broader ER and secretory homeostasis module rather than representing an isolated single-enzyme artifact.

story_title: Hspa5 perturbation induces a BiP-centered ER response with Hspa9-like features
proxy_summary: The Hspa5 transcript itself was not detectably depleted even where downstream ER-stress genes were induced.
proxy_why_it_matters: Direct target mRNA is therefore a poor engagement readout for this perturbation; the positive or neutral Hspa5 mRNA values are consistent with a buffered autoregulatory UPR target rather than a simple transcript knockdown signature.

story_title: Hnrnpc perturbation repeatedly shifts RNA-processing gene abundance across posterior neuronal classes
proxy_summary: The strongest Hnrnpc signature contains a mixed-direction RNA-splicing and nuclear-speck module.
proxy_why_it_matters: Up-regulation of Ddx39b, Ddx17, Srsf11, Pnn, Ncbp1 and related factors alongside repression of Rbm25, Luc7l2, Srsf2 and Tia1 connects the abundance signature to the established HNRNPC splice-regulatory axis while preserving that individual factors move in opposite directions.

story_title: Kdm5c, Nsd1, and Zmynd8 perturbations converge on a Ptgds-Capn3 thalamic response
proxy_summary: The main Zmynd8 response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was expressed through synaptic and neuronal-projection effector transcripts rather than through measured induction or repression of core NuRD subunit transcripts.
proxy_why_it_matters: ZMYND8 is a nuclear histone-reader and transcriptional regulator, but the cell-state output detected here was a neuronal receptor/adhesion/calcium module containing Gabbr2, Nrxn1, Grm1, Trim9, Lrrc7, P2rx7, Scn1b, and Cck.

story_title: Brd4 perturbation opposes synaptic-membrane and RNA-processing transcripts in thalamic neurons
proxy_summary: Across the responsive Brd4 signatures, Trrap and Yy1 were the most reproducible positive signature neighbors whereas assayed BRD4 interactor or disease-family chromatin genes such as Chd4, Nipbl, Smc1a, Smc3, Smarcb1, and Brd1 were much less Brd4-like in the main 151 population.
proxy_why_it_matters: This prioritizes an acetylation/coactivator and transcription-factor state linked to BRD4 transcriptional output over a generic chromatin-remodeler stress state, while also showing that not all physical or disease-neighbor chromatin perturbations are interchangeable in neurons.

story_title: Rbfox1 perturbation lowers an axonal and excitability transcript module
proxy_summary: Available LASR/RBP neighbor perturbations did not phenocopy Rbfox1; Hnrnpc, Hnrnpu, Hnrnph2, and Matr3 correlations with Rbfox1 were near zero in 151 and 155, and no unrestricted signature neighbor exceeded |r|=0.18.
proxy_why_it_matters: Membership in the same RNA-splicing assembly does not imply interchangeable abundance phenotypes, so Rbfox1-specific RNA recognition or isoform biology likely matters.

story_title: Sec63 perturbation induces ER-chaperone compensation not reproduced by other secretory-pathway perturbations
proxy_summary: Sec63 differed from multiple ER-adjacent secretory-pathway perturbations: Ssr4, Stt3b, Sec23a, and Sar1b showed self-depletion but did not induce Hspa5 in 151 or 155.
proxy_why_it_matters: The ER-stress response is linked to Sec63-mediated ER import rather than any perturbation of COPII export, OST activity, or TRAP/SSR-associated translocation components measured in the dataset.

story_title: ADNP perturbation produces a sparse CHD4-adjacent neuronal signature across thalamic, midbrain, caudal GABAergic, and Pvalb populations
proxy_summary: Arid2 diverged from Adnp in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut while Chd4 converged.
proxy_why_it_matters: This prevents over-generalizing ADNP loss as equivalent to any chromatin-remodeler perturbation and refines the SWI/SNF-related disease label toward a CHD4/ChAHP-biased state in this neuron class.

story_title: PPP2R1A perturbation defines a cortical Amy1-high, Rsrp1/Leng8-low reporter state without establishing a TSC or STXBP1 mechanism
proxy_summary: Ppp2r1a scaffold knockdown caused much larger transcriptional responses than knockdown of Ppp2r5d, Ppp2r2b, or Ptpa in matched cell classes.
proxy_why_it_matters: Human PPP2R1A and PPP2R5D are both PP2A neurodevelopmental-disorder genes, but the dataset shows that loss of the scaffold and loss of individual regulatory or activator components are not interchangeable in this short-term RNA assay.

story_title: Distinct endomembrane perturbations repeatedly enter a proteostasis neighborhood but do not form one interchangeable pathway
proxy_summary: Caml signatures weakly but recurrently resembled V-ATPase, clathrin/vesicle, and proteasome perturbations more than they showed any strong opposite neighbor.
proxy_why_it_matters: Direct WRB/ASNA1/GET-family comparisons were not available in the perturbation panel, but the nearest positive neighbors point to organelle acidification, vesicle traffic, and protein turnover machinery as transcriptomic neighbors of CAML loss in neurons.

story_title: KLF9 guides induce a Wsb1/Rasgrp2/Pld3 thalamic module not reproduced by KLF7 or KLF13
proxy_summary: Sin3a was the top positive restricted-signature neighbor of Klf9 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and shared several Klf9-induced genes.
proxy_why_it_matters: STRING places SIN3A near KLF9, so even a weak same-cell-type transcriptional convergence is mechanistically suggestive of a KLF9-corepressor axis worth testing directly.

story_title: ZMYM2 perturbation induces a compact Notum/Echdc2/F11r/Atp2a3 thalamic signature
proxy_summary: Zmym2 converged weakly but reproducibly with the chromatin-regulator perturbations Chd4 and Zmynd8 in 151 TH, whereas Sin3a was much broader and Rest and Sall4 were flat.
proxy_why_it_matters: This places the Zmym2 phenotype nearer to a selective ZMYND8/CHD4-like chromatin-remodeler axis than to every nuclear repressor assayed, preserving an informative distinction among related epigenetic perturbations.

story_title: SP4 perturbation is associated with a Tsga10/Abhd11/Svip module in posterior glutamatergic neurons
proxy_summary: The two active Sp4 signatures converged on an upregulated Tsga10/Abhd11-centered module, with Dnajc4, Svip, and Strada recurring at FDR or strong nominal support.
proxy_why_it_matters: The recurrence makes these genes better Sp4-response biomarkers than any one cell-type-specific hit and suggests that the active TH and MB glutamatergic responses share a noncanonical core.

story_title: ZFP148 perturbation lowers spliceosomal and synaptic-marker transcripts in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c neurons
proxy_summary: A weak but recurrent RNA-splicing signal centers on Srrm2, with Srrm2 nominally down in nine cell types and Srsf9/Luc7l2 down in the strongest 151 response.
proxy_why_it_matters: Zfp148 is annotated as a DNA-binding transcriptional regulator, so repeated depression of spliceosomal genes nominates RNA processing as a downstream neuronal module rather than merely isolated top genes.

story_title: NR2F1 perturbation couples Sorl1 induction to Sema7a repression in one thalamic neuronal population
proxy_summary: The close paralog Nr2f2 partially converged with Nr2f1 on Sorl1 induction in 151 cells, whereas Nr2f6 did not, and neither paralog phenocopied the full Sema7a-containing Nr2f1 signature.
proxy_why_it_matters: COUP-TFI/II homology does not translate into interchangeability in this neuronal state; Sorl1 appears to be the shared sensitive node while the rest of the Nr2f1 response is paralog-selective or guide-efficiency-limited.

story_title: KLF7 perturbation yields a single corrected Tuba1a decrease with a weaker cytoskeletal tail
proxy_summary: Klf9 was a weak inverse, not a phenocopy, of Klf7 in the Klf7-responsive thalamic class.
proxy_why_it_matters: KLF paralogs can have opposing axon-growth roles; the dataset preserves this non-interchangeability because Klf9 generated a stronger but distinct thalamic expression program.

story_title: GABRD perturbation produces a single Cttnbp2 increase in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c neurons
proxy_summary: In the thalamic class, Gabrb2, Gabra1, and Gabra4 were the nearest GABA-A-family neighbors of Gabrd, but other GABA-pathway perturbations and the top negative Grin1 neighbor were weak or anticorrelated.
proxy_why_it_matters: The result is qualitatively compatible with alpha/beta/delta receptor assembly but argues against treating all GABA-A receptor-related knockdowns as interchangeable transcriptomic perturbations.

story_title: A speculative ACSL4-to-SREBF2 feedback branch appears in superficial cortex but is supported by only one corrected sterol row
proxy_summary: The genes induced after Acsl4 knockdown are repressed by direct Srebf2 perturbation, placing the Acsl4 response on the activation side of the SREBP2 sterol program.
proxy_why_it_matters: The opposite polarity argues that Acsl4 loss is not phenocopying Srebf2 loss; instead, Acsl4 depletion appears to trigger a compensatory transcriptional program that Srebf2 normally drives.

story_title: TRRAP guides repress an imprinted and noncoding RNA module, but MYC silence does not establish a MYC-independent mechanism
proxy_summary: In mature neuronal cell types, Trrap perturbation did not significantly modulate a canonical MYC/E2F proliferation panel, and assayed Myc perturbation did not phenocopy Trrap.
proxy_why_it_matters: This separates the post-mitotic Trrap signature from the E2F cell-cycle program reported after Trrap deletion in neural progenitors.

story_title: GABRB2 and ATP2B1 perturbations reverse part of the ANK3 thalamic RNA state, but the shared excitability mechanism remains speculative
proxy_summary: Scn8a, Scn1b, and Fgf14 were weak but high-ranking same-direction signature neighbors of Ank3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
proxy_why_it_matters: The neighbor structure points back to the expected ankyrin-G/AIS sodium-channel neighborhood even though correlations were too modest to imply that sodium-channel loss alone explains the Ank3 signature.

story_title: KMT2D and KDM6A share the direction of a thalamic enhancer-associated marker set, but only the KMT2D arm is robust
proxy_summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Kdm6a converged with Kmt2d on a same-direction neuronal gene signature led by Ntng1, Nell1, Ptpn5, Cyp46a1, Tspan33, Thy1, and Mical2.
proxy_why_it_matters: KMT2D is the MLL4 catalytic subunit of a complex that can contain KDM6A, so this is the strongest positive dataset support for a biologically coherent KDM6A-MLL4 module in a defined adult neuronal class.

story_title: Rab7, Slc17a5, and Tsc1 perturbations share lysosomal and sterol RNA outputs, but the merged endolysosomal model overstates their equivalence
proxy_summary: Tsc1 was the nearest positive non-self Tsc2 neighbor in the main responsive classes, while Mtor and Rptor were inverse neighbors in 155 MB Glut and Mtor was the most anti-correlated perturbation in three responsive classes.
proxy_why_it_matters: The convergence with another TSC-complex subunit and opposition to the downstream kinase node verify the expected TSC-to-mTORC1 directionality at whole-transcriptome scale.

story_title: A lone Vegfa response after TFRC perturbation weakly suggests a neuronal low-iron compensation state
proxy_summary: Direct perturbations of iron-pathway genes did not strongly phenocopy Ireb2: Fth1 depletion was efficient but transcriptomically local, and the Tfrc perturbation was weak, although Tfrc was the closest Ireb2 signature neighbor in one thalamic class.
proxy_why_it_matters: IREB2 is upstream and post-transcriptional; loss of a ferritin subunit or a receptor transcript is therefore not interchangeable with partial loss of the RNA-binding regulator in this scRNA-seq assay.

story_title: FTO guides repeatedly lower Rsrp1, but a mechanistic bridge to spliceosome perturbations is unproven
proxy_summary: In 155 MB Glut, the Fto restricted signature was closest to spliceosome perturbations Prpf6 and Ddx23 and was opposite to Fus, with Rsrp1 moving in the same or opposite direction across those perturbations.
proxy_why_it_matters: This cross-perturbation geometry supports an RNA-processing module downstream of Fto in midbrain glutamatergic neurons and elevates Rsrp1 as a module readout rather than a one-off Fto hit.

story_title: WDFY3 guides suppress Jun, Stmn4, and synaptic transcripts in thalamic neurons, but the autophagy interpretation is unresolved
proxy_summary: Dctn1/Sema6a/Herc2/Pten were exploratory positive neighbors and Grin1 the strongest negative neighbor of the thalamic Wdfy3 signature, but whole-transcriptome correlations were modest.
proxy_why_it_matters: The top-neighbor scan points to candidate convergence and antagonism for follow-up while warning that restricted-signature correlations alone should not be treated as pathway identity.

story_title: KMT5B guides induce a small Ache/Syngap1/Grik1 thalamic signature despite no evidence of target-transcript loss
proxy_summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response links Kmt5b perturbation to a postsynaptic and translation-related gene module.
proxy_why_it_matters: Up-regulation of Ache, Syngap1, Grik1, near-threshold Nlgn2, Rab3a, Rab3gap2, and translation-initiation genes ties the strongest Kmt5b effect to neuronal communication rather than to a nonspecific chromatin-only readout.

story_title: PROX1 guides create a Tmem145/Vgf-high, Rreb1/Kcnd2-low thalamic state without demonstrating PROX1 loss
proxy_summary: In the responsive thalamic class, Prox1 guides induced a mixed neuronal and junctional module headed by Tmem145 and Vgf up-regulation and Rreb1 down-regulation.
proxy_why_it_matters: The strongest measured outputs provide concrete candidate biomarkers for the Prox1-responsive state and show that the effect is not a single-gene self change.

story_title: CREBBP guides produce an eight-gene thalamic state that EP300 does not reproduce, but paralog nonredundancy is not resolved
proxy_summary: Ddx17 and Srcap, transcripts encoding known CBP-interacting nuclear proteins, rose modestly in the same 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response.
proxy_why_it_matters: A small up-regulated nuclear branch could mark feedback onto CBP-associated RNA/chromatin machinery after Crebbp perturbation.

story_title: HNRNPU, U2AF2, and NAA15 signatures share modest spliceosome–proteasome neighbors without a common marker-defined mechanism
proxy_summary: Hnrnpu was not interchangeable with every STRING-linked hnRNP neighbor: Srsf1 and Rnpc3 were strong, whereas Hnrnpa1, Hnrnpa2b1, Hnrnph2, and Syncrip were weak in the same atlas.
proxy_why_it_matters: Close RNA-binding network membership should not be treated as functional redundancy in neuronal Perturb-seq; guide engagement and protein architecture can strongly gate responses.

story_title: GABRG2 perturbation weakly associates with a Bdnf/Vgf activity response in glutamatergic neurons
proxy_summary: The L4/5 Gabrg2 Bdnf signal lies in a restricted excitability signature neighborhood shared with Gphn and especially Kcnb1 perturbation.
proxy_why_it_matters: A weak Gabrg2 scalar phenotype becomes more interpretable when the same cell type shows a stronger Kcnb1-induced Bdnf/Vgf program and Gphn/Kcnb1 appear as the closest positive neighbors over the top Gabrg2 response genes.

story_title: LRP6 guides produce a weak Chgb/Nrbp2 thalamic response that does not establish canonical Wnt signaling or LRP5 divergence
proxy_summary: Within 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the Lrp6 signature converged with Ctnnb1 loss and opposed Apc loss, including the predicted decrease of Axin2 after Lrp6 or Ctnnb1 perturbation and increase after Apc perturbation.
proxy_why_it_matters: This ties the weak Lrp6 transcriptional phenotype to the canonical beta-catenin destruction-complex axis rather than to an unrelated thalamic stress signature.
